findings.title: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 floor for zero/negative-dimension inner vector, reopening the DoS
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 whenever an inner vector's Dimensions <= 0, because isVectorVariableLengthType recurses to the fixed leaf and the vec.Dimensions > 0 clause is skipped; a peer can pick that number to produce a 1 MB payload that allocates 26 MB, reopening the exact DoS the bound was written to close.

findings.title: Zero-VectorType test doesn't pin the panic its own comment says it prevents
findings.claim: The comment says the dim-0 carve-out exists so a caller-supplied zero VectorType cannot panic on the Scan goroutine, but the table only uses `var dst []float64`, which never touches SubType; with `var dst any` both rows still panic with a nil pointer dereference in VectorType.Zero(), since the new `t == nil` guard never runs for that destination type.

findings.title: "keep the name" fix applied to basic-type branch but not the VectorType branch with the same defect
findings.claim: NewCustomType(protoVer, TypeCustom, prefix+"VectorType") stores the bare prefix, so the PR's new error for a nested vector reads with no element type or dimension; storing `name` there instead would fix both the message and nested-vector decoding into interface{}, but the PR defers this to #1085 while adding a test that locks the bug in.

findings.title: "fewest bytes an element can occupy" is a lower bound, not a minimum; description's behavior claim only holds for fixed-size elements
findings.claim: For every variable-length type vectorElemMinSize returns 1 regardless of body, so a vector<smallint,4> can still decode a short/zero-length payload to garbage values instead of erroring; the description's claim that such payloads now error is true only for fixed-size elements like vector<int,3> and false for nine variable-length element types.

findings.title: "every path below turns it into an allocation" is false for the array path
findings.claim: *[N]T allocates nothing since marshal.go:1076 only compares rv.Len() != info.Dimensions, contradicting the stated rationale that the bound is purely an allocation guard, as the diff's own test comment elsewhere acknowledges.

findings.title: New guard discards the real underlying error and reports a wrong cause
findings.claim: VectorType.Zero() drops the underlying error `e`; the real cause is that VectorType never overrides NewWithError, but the guard reports a misleading message. Calling info.SubType.NewWithError() directly and wrapping the returned error would report the real reason.

findings.title: Saturating-multiply branch has no test coverage
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize measures 92.3% coverage; the uncovered block is exactly `return math.MaxInt32`, the subtlest new line guarding a peer-supplied inner dimension, and needs a test like vector<vector<float,1<<40>,…> to cover it.

findings.title: Asymmetric error messages: short payload loses exact byte count, surplus payload keeps it
findings.claim: A short payload's error loses the exact byte count ("3 dimensions do not fit in 4 bytes") while a surplus payload's error keeps it ("expected 12 bytes, got 16"); including elemMin in the message would restore the arithmetic symmetry.

findings.title: Test comment claims "eight bytes" per inner vector when it's actually four, contradicting another line
findings.claim: "Eight bytes" is wrong per inner vector since each is actually four (1 prefix + 3 zero vints); eight is only the total for the two the subtest marshals, contradicting line 660 where the same shape is costed at 4.

findings.title: "not parallel" test rationale misnames the actual mechanism it's protecting against
findings.claim: The comment's rationale is wrong because Go never runs a serial top-level test concurrently with parallel ones; the real exposure is leaked goroutines from earlier networked tests in the package, and a reader could "fix" this by mistakenly adding t.Parallel().

findings.title: Test's payload/8 budget is fragile relative to fixed overhead below ~32KB
findings.claim: The payload/8 budget is coupled to payload against ~3 KB of fixed overhead, so below ~32 KB the test fails for unrelated reasons; an absolute budget would be sturdier.

findings.title: Claim that a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes has a stated counterexample
findings.claim: The unconditional claim is false because vector<vector<float,0>,N> encodes to zero bytes and the bound does narrow there, making the statement degenerate but still incorrect as written.

findings.title: Identical condition evaluated twice in a row
findings.claim: The identical `info.Dimensions > 0 && data != nil` check appears at both marshal.go:998 and marshal.go:1007 and should be merged into one block.

findings.title: No dimension-bound test goes through the public Unmarshal with a readTypeInfo-parsed type, though that's the stated threat model
findings.claim: No dimension-bound row in the 587-690 table goes through the public Unmarshal with a readTypeInfo-parsed type, even though the stated threat model is Scan's goroutine and the file already has wireVectorType available to do this.

findings.title: PR body includes a Claude Code attribution line, against the user's conventions
findings.claim: The PR body carries a "🤖 Generated with Claude Code" line, which the reviewer notes goes against the user's conventions forbidding such attribution in PR descriptions.

findings.title: names[1] panics on a truncated vector spec, same crash class this PR exists to fix, unaddressed
findings.claim: names[1] panics with an index-out-of-range error on a truncated vector spec such as ...VectorType(...FloatType); it's reachable via asVectorType → goType → NewWithError → Iter.Scan, which is unrecovered — the same crash class this PR exists to fix, left unaddressed in the function it edits.

findings.title: dim, _ := strconv.Atoi(...) drops ErrRange, silently turning an overflowing dimension into MaxInt64
findings.claim: frame.go:861 discards ErrRange from strconv.Atoi, so an overflowing dimension becomes MaxInt64 and the operator never learns what string the server actually sent; helpers.go:222/267 still degrade to a nameless custom() on parse failure, now inconsistent with the change at helpers.go:279.

findings.title: #1106: vint length narrowing to negative makes vector<text,1> decode [""] with nil error
findings.claim: The reviewer confirms this issue (tracked as #1106) is reachable as described, but states it is correctly scoped out of this PR.

findings.title: #1086: surplus trailing bytes silently dropped in the generic path while fast paths reject them
findings.claim: The reviewer confirms this issue (tracked as #1086) is reachable as described, but states it is correctly scoped out of this PR.
